question.prompt: Andy and Betsy both live in Mathville. Andy leaves Mathville on his bicycle at \(1{:}30,\) traveling due north at a steady \(8\) miles per hour. Betsy leaves on her bicycle from the same point at \(2{:}30,\) traveling due east at a steady \(12\) miles per hour. At what time will they be exactly the same distance from their common starting point?

solutions.title: Equate the riding distances
solutions.explanation:
Each rider travels straight away from the starting point, so each rider's distance from it is speed times riding time. Andy has ridden for one hour longer than Betsy.

Let \(t\) be the number of hours Andy has ridden when their distances are equal. Betsy has then ridden for \(t-1\) hours, so
\[
8t=12(t-1).
\]
Expanding and solving,
\[
8t=12t-12,\qquad 4t=12,\qquad t=3.
\]
Three hours after \(1{:}30\) is \(\boxed{4{:}30}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
